source_title: See the Original A Nightmare on Elm Street Cast Side-by-Side with the Stars from the 2010 Remake - People.com
source_excerpt:
Robert Englund originated iconic villain Freddy Krueger in the 1984 film, and the character was later brought to life by Jackie Earle Haley
Robert Englund originated Freddy Krueger in A Nightmare on Elm Street , while Jackie Earle Haley played the villain in the 2010 remake
Heather Langenkamp and Rooney Mara portrayed different versions of heroine Nancy in the two films
Johnny Depp made his feature film debut in the 1984 horror classic as Nancy’s boyfriend, Glen
A Nightmare on Elm Street launched one of the most iconic horror movie franchises of all time when it premiered back in 1984.
The film follows sadistic child slasher Freddy Krueger ( Robert Englund ), who was burned alive by his present-day victims’ parents. He returns to stalk the town’s local teens — including heroine Nancy Thompson ( Heather Langenkamp ) — in their dreams.
Following the success of the original film, eight more movies were made, including a 2010 remake with an all-new cast. In July 2026, The Hollywood Reporter revealed that a new installment based on the original screenplay is in the works. The U.S. rights to the reboot are being licensed by late original director Wes Craven ’s estate, which includes his widow, Iya Labunka, and his son, Jonathan Craven.
Ahead, see the original A Nightmare on Elm Street cast side-by-side with the stars from the 2010 remake.
Robert Englund and Jackie Earle Haley as Freddy Krueger
Larry Busacca/WireImage; New Line/Kobal/Shutterstock
Recognizable by his red and green striped sweater, fedora and signature leather glove with metal blades, Freddy was originally brought to life by Englund before Jackie Earle Haley took over for the 2010 remake.
In October 2024, Englund told PEOPLE that he knew he found Krueger the moment he saw his silhouette in a mirror.
“ I remember ... seeing [myself] and getting the idea ,” he said. “Because of the overhead lighting, once I had that hat on and the glove, I saw the shadow. I saw the Freddy silhouette in the shadow and I went, ‘Aha, this is something I can work with. This is something I can exploit.’ ”
Heather Langenkamp and Rooney Mara as Nancy Thompson/Nancy Holbrook
Langenkamp’s Nancy is an ordinary teenage girl who uses her sharp intellect to outsmart Freddy in the 1984 film. In the 2010 remake, the character is reimagined as Nancy Holbrook, played by Rooney Mara . While both characters end up defeating Freddy in the end, their personalities and methods of success vary.
In an October 2024 interview with PEOPLE, Langenkamp admitted that she was terrified of Freddy while filming.
“I hadn’t seen Robert in makeup for several days and I went into the [high school] scene where Tina [Amanda Wyss] leads me down into the boiler room and I got down there and I saw Freddy for the first time,” she said.
Englund was wearing “the shadow with the hat, the sweater, the boots and the glove.” She added, “It was really striking and I knew at the moment he was terrifying. I never had to act that part because he was always terrifying to me.”
Johnny Depp and Kyle Gallner as Glen Lantz/Quentin Smith
New Line Cinema/Courtesy Everett Collection; New Line Cinema via Alamy
A Nightmare on Elm Street marked Johnny Depp ’s feature film debut, where he played Glen Lantz, Nancy’s level-headed boyfriend. In a September 2015 interview with Variety following Craven’s death at 76, Depp reflected on his experience with the director.
“Wes Craven was the guy who gave me my start, from my perspective, for almost no reason in particular,” he said.
“I read scenes with his daughter when I auditioned for the part. At the time, I was a musician. I wasn’t really acting. It was not anything very near to my brain or my heart, which is pretty much how it remains to this day,” the actor continued. “But Wes Craven was brave enough to give me the gig based on his daughter’s opinion. I guess she had read with a bunch of actors, and after the casting sessions, she said, ‘No, that’s the guy.’ ”
In the 2010 remake, the character of Glen Lantz is reimagined as Quentin Smith (Kyle Gallner). Both Glen and Quentin play Nancy’s love interest, but they meet very different fates. While Depp’s character falls victim to Freddy, Gallner’s character survives his final confrontation with the villain.
Amanda Wyss and Katie Cassidy as Christina Gray/Kris Fowles
Played by Amanda Wyss in the original film, Christina “Tina” Gray is Nancy’s close friend — and Freddy’s first victim. She suffers from horrifying dreams involving a burned man with a razor glove, only to find out that Nancy is having those same dreams. Her death triggers the main plot of the film, leading to her boyfriend’s wrongful arrest and Nancy’s battle against Freddy.
In the 2010 remake, Tina Gray’s character is reimagined as Kris Fowles ( Katie Cassidy ). Both Tina and Kris are friends with Nancy in their respective films, but Kris is Freddy’s second victim instead of his first.
Jsu Garcia and Thomas Dekker as Rod Lane/Jesse Braun
Rod Lane becomes a prime suspect in the 1984 film after witnessing his girlfriend Tina’s violent murder in her sleep. Played by Jsu Garcia, the rebellious character panics and bolts away before the police can arrest him.
In the 2010 remake, Rod Lane is reimagined as Jesse Braun — Kris’ ex-boyfriend — and portrayed by Heroes actor Thomas Dekker. While their relationships with Tina and Kris differ, both Rod and Jesse are accused of their murders and eventually fall victim to Freddy while locked up in their jail cells.
Ronee Blakley and Connie Britton as Marge Thompson/Gwen Holbrook
Ronee Blakley plays Marge Thompson, Nancy’s mother, in 1984’s A Nightmare on Elm Street . In the 2010 remake, Marge’s character is reimagined as Dr. Gwen Holbrook and played by Connie Britton .
Both Marge and Gwen harbor a secret from their daughter Nancy — namely, that they were a part of the group of parents who tracked down Freddy and burned him alive.
John Saxon and Clancy Brown as Donald Thompson/Alan Smith
In the original film, Donald Thompson (John Saxon) is Nancy’s lieutenant father and Marge’s ex-husband, who also participated in burning Freddy alive. He dismisses Nancy’s warnings about Freddy.
The character is reimagined as Alan Smith in the 2010 remake. Portrayed by Clancy Brown , Alan is the father of Quentin, Nancy’s love interest. Both characters are police officers who remain skeptical of the teens’ claims that Freddy has returned to terrorize them.
